package: SMD module, 25.5 x 18.0 x 3.1 mm body, 41 pads (40 castellated edge pads + EPAD)
description: Espressif ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n + Bluetooth LE 5 module built on an ESP32-S3 SoC (Xtensa dual-core 32-bit LX7, up to 240 MHz), 384 KB ROM, 512 KB SRAM, 16 KB RTC SRAM, 8 MB Quad SPI flash on module, NO PSRAM, 40 MHz crystal, on-module PCB antenna (the -1U variant substitutes a u.FL connector). 36 GPIOs brought out. Source: Espressif ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 & WROOM-1U Datasheet v1.8 (2026-03-02).

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Table 3-1 type P. Corner pad nearest the PCB antenna / keepout zone (Figure 3-1).

pinout.name: 3V3
pinout.notes: Table 3-1 type P, 'Power supply'. Sole supply pin of the module. Recommended operating 3.0-3.6 V (Table 6-2); external supply must be able to deliver at least 0.5 A (IVDD, Table 6-2).

pinout.name: EN
pinout.notes: Table 3-1 type I. High: on, enables the chip. Low: off, the chip powers off. Datasheet states: 'Do not leave the EN pin floating.' Recommended RC delay circuit at EN: R = 10 kohm pull-up to 3V3 and C = 1 uF to GND (Section 9 note, Figure 9-1 R1/C2). Power-up timing: tSTBL min 50 us for the rails to stabilise before EN is pulled high; tRST min 50 us for EN to stay below VIL_nRST to reset the chip (Table 4-6).

pinout.name: IO3
pinout.notes: RTC_GPIO3, GPIO3, TOUCH3, ADC1_CH2. STRAPPING PIN (JTAG signal source select, Section 4.4). Default configuration per Table 4-1 is 'Floating' with no bit value: this pin has NO internal pull resistors and the datasheet states the strapping value 'must be controlled by the external circuit that cannot be in a high impedance state'. Combined with EFUSE_DIS_PAD_JTAG / EFUSE_DIS_USB_JTAG / EFUSE_STRAP_JTAG_SEL per Table 4-5; with all eFuses at their default 0, GPIO3 is Ignored and JTAG comes from the USB Serial/JTAG controller.

pinout.name: IO46
pinout.notes: GPIO46. STRAPPING PIN (chip boot mode with GPIO0, Section 4.1; and ROM message printing, Section 4.3). Default per Table 4-1: weak pull-down, bit value 0. Boot mode table 4-3: SPI Boot needs GPIO0 = 1 (GPIO46 any value); Joint Download Boot needs GPIO0 = 0 AND GPIO46 = 0. Table 3-1 lists no alternate functions beyond GPIO46.

pinout.name: IO47
pinout.notes: SPICLK_P_DIFF, GPIO47, SUBSPICLK_P_DIFF (bold default GPIO47). Table 3-1 footnote c: only for modules embedded with ESP32-S3R16V is the VDD_SPI voltage 1.8 V, making GPIO47/GPIO48 a 1.8 V domain. The -N8 SKU has NO PSRAM and is not an R16V part, so on this part IO47 operates in the normal 3.3 V domain.

pinout.name: IO48
pinout.notes: SPICLK_N_DIFF, GPIO48, SUBSPICLK_N_DIFF (bold default GPIO48). See IO47 note: 1.8 V operation applies only to R16V modules, not to -N8; IO48 is 3.3 V here.

pinout.name: IO45
pinout.notes: GPIO45. STRAPPING PIN (VDD_SPI voltage select, Section 4.2). Default per Table 4-1: weak pull-down, bit value 0 -> VDD_SPI = 3.3 V from VDD3P3_RTC via RSPI. CRITICAL for this SKU: the Section 8 Module Schematics note states that for modules WITHOUT PSRAM (which includes -N8) 'please ensure that GPIO45 is not pulled high when the module is powered up by the external circuit' - pulling it high at power-up would select the 1.8 V flash regulator and prevent the module booting. Table 3-1 lists no alternate functions beyond GPIO45.

pinout.name: IO0
pinout.notes: RTC_GPIO0, GPIO0. STRAPPING PIN (chip boot mode, Section 4.1). Default per Table 4-1: weak pull-up, bit value 1 -> SPI Boot (normal run). Drive/strap low together with GPIO46 = 0 for Joint Download Boot (USB-Serial-JTAG, USB-OTG or UART download). Figure 9-1 fits it as a 2-pin 'Boot Option' header JP4 to GND.

pinout.name: IO35
pinout.notes: SPIIO6, GPIO35, FSPID, SUBSPID. Table 3-1 footnote a: for pins 28-30 the default function is decided by an eFuse bit. Footnote b: IO35/36/37 are connected to the Octal SPI PSRAM and NOT available for other uses ONLY on modules embedded with ESP32-S3R8 or ESP32-S3R16V. The -N8 SKU carries a plain ESP32-S3 with no PSRAM, so IO35 IS AVAILABLE as a general-purpose IO on this part.

pinout.name: IO36
pinout.notes: SPIIO7, GPIO36, FSPICLK, SUBSPICLK. See IO35 note: available on -N8 (footnote b restriction applies only to R8/R16V Octal-PSRAM modules). Default function decided by eFuse bit (footnote a).

pinout.name: EPAD
pinout.notes: Table 3-1 type P, function GND. Central exposed thermal pad. Section 9: soldering the EPAD to the base-board ground is NOT mandatory, but it optimises thermal performance; if soldered, use the correct amount of paste - too much raises the module off the board and degrades the adhesion of the other pads.

decoupling.placement: bulk capacitor on the 3V3 rail feeding the module
decoupling.notes: Figure 9-1 Peripheral Schematics: C1 = 22 uF from VDD33 to GND. This is the only bulk value the datasheet states for the module.

decoupling.placement: close to pin 2 (3V3), in parallel with the 22 uF bulk
decoupling.notes: Figure 9-1: C3 = 0.1 uF from VDD33 to GND.

decoupling.placement: EN to GND, forming an RC delay with a 10 kohm pull-up from EN to 3V3
decoupling.notes: Section 9 note (verbatim intent): 'To ensure that the power supply to the ESP32-S3 chip is stable during power-up, it is advised to add an RC delay circuit at the EN pin. The recommended setting for the RC delay circuit is usually R = 10 kohm and C = 1 uF.' Specific values should be adjusted to the module power-up timing and the chip power-up/reset sequence (Section 4.5: tSTBL min 50 us, tRST min 50 us). Corresponds to R1/C2 in Figure 9-1.

decoupling.placement: EN to GND, in parallel with the reset pushbutton
decoupling.notes: Figure 9-1 optional reset circuit: pushbutton SW1 from EN to GND with C8 = 0.1 uF in parallel and R7 = 0 ohm in series to EN. Only needed if a reset button is fitted; it is in addition to the 1 uF RC delay cap.

land_pattern.notes: From Figure 11-1 'ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 Recommended PCB Land Pattern' (units mm). Pad count 41 = 40 perimeter pads + 1 central thermal land. Perimeter pads: 40 x 1.5 mm (radial length) by 0.9 mm (width), 1.27 mm pitch. Land pattern envelope 18 wide x 25.5 long, matching the module body. Pad numbering per Figure 3-1: pins 1-15 down one long side, 15-26 along the short side opposite the antenna, 26-40 up the other long side; pin 1 and pin 40 are the two pads closest to the antenna end. Stated figure dimensions: 18 (width), 25.5 (length), 16.51 (span of a side pad row, = 13 x 1.27), 17.5 (span across the pad field at the antenna-opposite end), 2.015 (twice, along the short row), 0.5, 1.27, 7.49 (module top edge to the start of the pads), 6 (Antenna Area depth), 10.29 and 7.5 (locating the thermal land), 3.7 x 3.7 (thermal land array extent), 0.9 (thermal land sub-pad size). ANTENNA AREA: the top 18 x 6 mm of the land pattern is drawn as 'Antenna Area' and carries no copper - see layout_notes. Module body (Figure 10-1): 18.0 +/-0.2 x 25.5 +/-0.2 x 3.1 +/-0.15 mm; module-side castellated pads are 40 x 0.85 x 0.9 mm on 1.27 mm pitch with 40 x dia 0.55 mm castellated half-holes. row_spacing_mm deliberately omitted: Figure 11-1 dimensions the pad field as a 17.5 mm outer span, not as a row centre-to-centre value.

layout_notes: ANTENNA KEEPOUT (module side, datasheet Figure 11-1 and Figure 10-1): the PCB antenna occupies the last 6 mm of the module's 25.5 mm length, across its full 18 mm width. Figure 11-1 labels this 18 x 6 mm rectangle 'Antenna Area' and shows it free of copper; Figure 3-1 labels the same region 'Keepout Zone'. Pins 1 and 40 are the pads immediately adjacent to it.

ANTENNA KEEPOUT (base-board side): this datasheet does not dimension the base-board keepout - it defers to 'ESP32-S3 Hardware Design Guidelines > General Principles of PCB Layout for Modules' (note under Figure 3-1 and Section 11.2). The bullets below marked [HDG] are transcribed from that document (Espressif ESP32-S3 Hardware Design Guidelines, release master, Section 1.4.7, Figures 24-26), which is a separate PDF from the datasheet.

[HDG] Preferred placement: 'It is suggested to place the module's on-board PCB antenna outside the base board, and the feed point of the antenna close to the edge of the base board.' Figures 24/25 mark only the corner positions (antenna fully overhanging a board edge) with a check mark as strongly recommended; mid-edge and interior positions are marked as not recommended.

[HDG] Fallback if the antenna cannot extend beyond the board edge: keep the feed point as close to the board edge as possible, then 'cut off the base board on both sides of the antenna and below it' to minimise the effect of the board material and give the antenna a large clearance area. The module must NOT be placed in the centre of the board with clearance hollowed out on all four sides.

[HDG] Clearance-area dimensions, Figure 26 'Keepout Zone for ESP32-S3 Module's Antenna': the cut-out is 6 mm deep (the antenna depth), extends Min 15 mm laterally on the antenna feed-point side, and leaves at most Max 2 mm of base board laterally on the far side and at most Max 1 mm of base board overlapping the antenna depthwise.

[HDG] 'Sufficient ground copper and dense ground vias should be placed on the base board near the antenna' - i.e. ground the board right up to the clearance boundary, but keep the clearance area itself clear of board material.

[HDG] End-product/housing: a clearance of at least 15 mm is recommended in all directions around the PCB antenna inside the housing. The finished product should be tested for throughput and communication range to confirm RF performance.

[HDG] The USB port, any USB-to-serial chip and all UART signal lines (traces, vias, test points, header pins) must be kept as far away from the antenna as possible. UART traces should be surrounded by ground copper and ground vias.
[HDG] The RF antenna should be placed away from high-frequency components such as crystals, DDR SDRAM and high-frequency clocks; no high-frequency signal traces should run close to the RF path.

[HDG] USB routing: use a 90 ohm +/-10% differential pair, route the two traces in parallel at equal length, minimise via transitions (add a pair of ground return vias at each transition if unavoidable), keep a continuous ground reference layer beneath, and surround the pair with ground copper. Reserve space for series resistors/capacitors on the USB traces near the chip.

EN: do not leave floating (Table 3-1). Fit the recommended RC delay (10 kohm to 3V3, 1 uF to GND) so the rails are stable before EN releases; tSTBL min 50 us before EN goes high, tRST min 50 us below VIL_nRST to force a reset (Table 4-6).

Strapping-pin timing (Table 4-2 / Figure 4-1): setup time tSU min 0 ms before EN is pulled high; hold time tH min 3 ms after EN is high, during which the strapping levels must be held before the pins revert to normal IO. Any external circuit driving a strapping pin must respect the 3 ms hold.

Strapping summary (Table 4-1): GPIO0 weak pull-up (default 1), GPIO45 weak pull-down (default 0), GPIO46 weak pull-down (default 0), GPIO3 floating with NO internal pull - GPIO3 must be driven by a non-high-impedance external circuit if its strap is used. All four latch their value at reset and are then free as ordinary IO.
GPIO45 must not be pulled high at power-up on this no-PSRAM SKU (Section 8 note) - it would force VDD_SPI to 1.8 V and the 3.3 V flash would not boot.

EPAD (pin 41) soldering is optional but improves thermal performance; if soldered, control paste volume so the module does not stand off the board. Figure 11-1 shows the thermal land as a 3 x 3 array of 0.9 mm pads inside a 3.7 x 3.7 mm area, each with a 'Via for thermal pad'.

Module placement/handling: MSL 3, store < 40 C / 90% RH, solder within 168 h of opening the moisture barrier bag or bake. Single reflow only; peak 235-250 C, peak time 30-70 s, > 217 C for 60-90 s, SAC lead-free (Section 12).

Supply sizing: the external 3V3 supply must be able to deliver at least 0.5 A (IVDD, Table 6-2). Measured peaks are 355 mA (Wi-Fi TX 802.11b 1 Mbps @20.5 dBm) and 344 mA (Bluetooth LE TX @20.0 dBm) at 3.3 V / 25 C, 100% TX duty cycle (Tables 6-4, 6-5).

Availability of IOs on this SKU: the module brings out GPIO0-GPIO21, GPIO35-GPIO42, GPIO43 (TXD0), GPIO44 (RXD0), and GPIO45-GPIO48 - 36 GPIOs in total. GPIO22 through GPIO34 appear nowhere in Table 3-1 and are therefore not available on any module pad; the chip-side SPI bus that the on-module 8 MB Quad SPI flash consumes (SPICLK, SPICS0, SPID, SPIQ, SPIWP, SPIHD - U1 pins 30-35 driving U2 in Figure 8-1) is internal to the module and is not exposed. This datasheet does not print GPIO numbers for those internal flash pins.

IO35/IO36/IO37 (pins 28/29/30) ARE usable on -N8: Table 3-1 footnote b withholds them only on ESP32-S3R8 / ESP32-S3R16V modules where they wire to Octal SPI PSRAM. -N8 has no PSRAM. Their default function is set by an eFuse bit (footnote a).
IO47/IO48 (pins 24/25) are 3.3 V on -N8; the 1.8 V VDD_SPI domain of footnote c applies only to R16V modules.
